title: ai that watches you game and reacts in real time (experimenting with an AI gameplay layer)
author: ivyleaguedegen
selftext:
been building a project called navi and thought this sub might find it interesting since it sits at the intersection of ai and game experience.

just to clarify upfront, this isn’t a game itself. it’s something that runs alongside existing games as a separate layer.

the idea i’ve been exploring is what happens if you move beyond scripted or prompt-based interactions and instead have something that reacts to gameplay in real time. it watches the screen and generates voice responses as things happen, so if a player dies, clutches, or discovers something, it reacts without needing explicit input.

you can still talk back with push to talk or voice, but the system doesn’t depend on that to stay active.

right now the focus is mostly on fun and entertainment, just making solo gameplay feel more alive rather than trying to coach or optimize performance. coaching is something i’m interested in exploring later, but it’s not the priority yet.

a lot of the work so far has gone into making this feel coherent instead of random. latency is critical since reactions need to land at the right moment, and i’ve been experimenting with persistent memory and layered personality design so responses feel consistent over time.

i’m curious how people here think about this kind of system. does an external, real-time reactive layer feel like a meaningful direction for ai in games, or does it risk being more distracting than useful?

it’s still early, but i’ve got a small alpha up if anyone wants to try it: [http://heynavi.gg/](http://heynavi.gg/)

would really appreciate feedback from people building in this space or thinking about ai-driven game experiences

comments.author: krazyjakee
comments.body:
Great concept!  
  
The "I see it" and other pretexts seems like a bug from a flawed prompt. That is going to get annoying fast.

replies.author: ivyleaguedegen
replies.body: Thanks! Definitely constantly fine tuning the prompts to make each character distinct and having the AI behave in the best possible way for a majority of users. Finally have some users testing now so im adjusting accordingly!

comments.author: Natural-Rich6
comments.body:
Is so a irritated 😠 
Like shut up I play to realex not for some ai to drill in my heAd

replies.author: ivyleaguedegen
replies.body:
Definitely not going for that. Still early so it’s pretty bare bones but im tryna add a leveling system and like an idle game on top.  

I’m going for more like a meta-game type vibe. Kind of a guiding principle im using as i build this is what would it be like if Link/Jett/insert ur favorite video game character could go with you into different game worlds.

I also would really like to build some functionality into the tool soon too. Don’t want to get too unfocused in terms of what the actual product does but there’s a lot of cool AI tools and agents trying to make people’s work life better, I’d love to add in features that make people’s recreational computer life better: Spotify integrations, discord integrations, maybe using what it knows about you to recommend video games/songs/youtube videos you might like etc. idk i have a lot of ideas.

But i see it more along the lines of a YouTube video or twitch stream ppl put on in the background while they game, except this is contextual and is reacting to your game world rather than being totally removed. Hard coded in the prompts to never try to claim and act like a real friend and if asked to be up front what it is: an AI that reacts to your game. Definitely one of the most important things to me

replies.author: platypus-3fh98hhwefd
replies.body:
The question is: *why would you even want* an AI to react to your gameplay

It's not a person, it doesn't have real opinions. This usecase is explicitly meant to *simulate* those things, hence "friendship simulator". You're literally asking for its input/what it "thinks" in your examples here, and LLMs are notorious for just being sycophantic. Attaching a voice & visual avatar only serves to increase the user's inclination to personify the LLM, when it should simply be a tool

It's TikTokification, engagement for engagement's sake. not providing material value

replies.author: ivyleaguedegen
replies.body:
I get what you’re saying. I think it could be a bunch of things. Some people admittedly have been using it as a “friendship simulators”, other people have been using it as an assistant/coach to remember things while they play, other people have used it as kind of like an instructor or teacher to learn in game lore or history depending on the game they’re playing.

Ofc I want to create a product that has the correct guardrails in place so people don’t build unhealthy relationships with these AI and I would never want ppl to fall into AI psychosis with these tools. In this alpha I’ve built tools to ensure that, and as more ppl use it I’ll continue to use feedback to champion that.

With that being said, I think there’s a lot of different use cases. I’m not here to dictate how users use the tool however. I dont think theres a single way users could or should use it. I’ve just noticed so many ppl building AI tools around productivity. I wanted to try building something for the other, more leisure part of our life.

Ofc appreciate and respect your opinions, as these questions are critical and really matter as I continue to build this product. Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts 🙏🏽

I plan on making a local version honestly. Like tymuska said you’ll need good hardware to run a strong enough parameter model with a video game and not see performance dips, but it’s definitely possible.

I’ll prob open source a good bit of the code base soon too. I’m just trying to get the core product into a good state before that.

Also in terms of minutes it’s an hour a day and recharges daily so even right now you should be able to play a good bit! (easy on me tho im paying for all the api cost out of pocket haha)

Dont really know how it works, but im guessing ElevenLabs. Maybe you could add an option to replace the voice with other API. I might be talking bs, so dont mind me haha

replies.author: ivyleaguedegen
replies.body:
Oh not sure if there’s local alternatives tbh. I know the folks at r/sillytavern have a lot of cool open source local projects though! Not sure if they function quite like this though. 

I actually use inworld AI for the voices, they’re my favorite TTS api and started off as AI generated NPC voices for video games so I thought they were the most fitting haha. Definitely looking to add more voices and stuff, not sure if I’ll add capability to switch APIs on the product as I don’t want to over complicate it for non technical people, but I’ll prob eventually open source a large part of the project outside of the characters so ppl will be able to switch API keys and do whatever they want then.

comments.author: interestingsystems
comments.body: I love the idea, but I think there's a different place to apply this. I don't want to banter with a bot, and for fast paced games I know the bot doesn't actually have a clue what I'm doing because of the screenshot cadence. But if I was playing something less twitch based, it would be pretty sweet to chat with something that could help me, or that would add lore about the world from what it knows based on something I'm looking at or doing in the moment. Think Skyrim if the bot was helping me finish a quest, or giving me some more lore on a character. Something more like your last example.

replies.author: ivyleaguedegen
replies.body: Oh that’s pretty sick. Yeah I’ve been testing it with quicker paced games, but an example i didn’t include in here was total war and CK3 (I’m actually a strategy game guy myself). I actually was asking it questions about the 3 Kingdoms period of China and the Philippines circa. 1000 (shoutout all under Heaven dlc for those that play ck3) and it was giving some pretty cool insights. It works for every game essentially, but i am tweaking the behavior depending on the type of game. So its behavior in a fast paced shooter vs a strategy game will prob continue to change over time.

replies.author: interestingsystems
replies.body: Yeah exactly, it sounds great for strategy games!

comments.author: tymuska
comments.body: About how much of your apps infrastructure is local vs online (TTS, STT, LLM, etc.)?

replies.author: ivyleaguedegen
replies.body:
Rn it’s all cloud. I have two worker LLMs that feed the main LLM input on the users mood and screen that are running on the cloud too that I’m gonna move over to local pretty soon. STT is with deepgram, TTS in inworld (although I’m gonna collapse both to inworld soon to improve latency)

Long term I def want an all local option as ik that’s important to ppl (might keep STT cloud for character consistency) but prob still a few months out for that. Pricing would also prob be different since ppl are doing the inference themselves
